newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russian '96 wheat output seen up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russian '96 wheat output seen up 15 pct.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
SOVECON SEES RUSSIA'S 1996 WHEAT OUTPUT AT 34.6 MLN TNS
MOSCOW, Nov 27 - Russia's 1996 wheat output is estimated to increase by about 15 percent on last year's drought-hit output.
Again, SovEcon's current estimates are very close to those given earlier in the crop year.
In most regions, the Russian wheat harvest has declined on the 1991-1995 average, particularly in the Northern Caucasus.
In this region, the most important wheat surplus area in the country, wheat output slumped to 7.4 million tonnes, down from 14.6 million tonnes last year and 19.3 million in 1991-95.
In addition, only 30 percent of the harvested wheat is estimated to be of milling quality.
As a result, the Northern Caucasus may sharply cut its deliveries to wheat-consuming regions in the European part of Russia.
Given that, import demand by these provinces for milling wheat and flour in 1996/97 is likely to increase.
